CausalChain: Chronic inflammation → Increased IL-6 production → Activation of JAK → Phosphorylation and dimerization of STAT3 → Transcription of oncogenic and survival genes along with epigenetic repression of SOCS3 → Loss of negative feedback on IL-6/STAT3 signaling → Sustained STAT3 signaling and tumorigenesis. Restoring SOCS3 expression would reinstate negative regulation, disrupt this loop, and counteract HCC progression.
Hypothesis: Epigenetic reactivation of SOCS3 in HCC cells will restore negative feedback on the IL-6/STAT3 signaling pathway, leading to reduced tumor proliferation, invasion, and drug resistance, especially when used in combination with IL-6/STAT3 inhibitors.
Abstract: This review proposes a novel therapeutic strategy for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) that centers on the epigenetic reactivation of negative regulators of the IL-6/STAT3 signaling axis, particularly SOCS3. Chronic inflammation and persistent IL-6 exposure drive robust activation of the JAK/STAT3 pathway, which in turn fuels oncogenic processes such as proliferation, angiogenesis, immune evasion, and acquisition of cancer stem cell properties in HCC. However, this pathway is normally counterbalanced by negative regulators like SOCS3, whose expression is often epigenetically suppressed in the tumorous microenvironment. By targeting the epigenetic mechanisms that silence SOCS3, it may be possible to restore its negative feedback, suppress STAT3 hyperactivation, and thereby inhibit tumor progression and enhance the effectiveness of combination therapies.
